notes: Read docs/SPEC.md, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md and docs/research/tech-reference.md before starting any task.

The foundation is split: 'foundation' (F0, the foundation object) runs alone first and creates every shared file, every contract stub and every placeholder; then foundation-ui (F1), foundation-auth (F2) and foundation-platform (F3) run in parallel with slot-engine. Every other module depends on F1, F2 and F3 directly or through its dependencies (booking-core needs only F3 and slot-engine).

ownedPaths are disjoint across the foundation and all modules. Files listed in foundation.handover are created by the foundation (stubs or placeholders) and then belong exclusively to the listed module.
dependsOn lists modules that must be finished first; all other cross-module calls go through the typed stubs of ARCHITECTURE section 25, so modules without a dependency edge can run concurrently.

Run at most maxConcurrentAgents (4) agents at once on the 4 vCPU / 15 GB build machine. The modules array is in recommended scheduling order (a topological order that front-loads the critical path); when several modules are ready, start them in array order.

Every heavy command (next dev, next start, next build, Playwright, tsc, next typegen) goes through scripts/heavy.sh, which allows two concurrent holders per slot (ARCHITECTURE 26 rule 18). typecheck:owned uses per-module incremental build info in .cache/.

Contract churn rule (ARCHITECTURE 26 rule 17): implement in new files and switch contract re-exports only when green; a contract file must compile at every moment. Integration tests vi.mock other modules' contracts.
Race-safety tests live in *.pg.test.ts and run on real Postgres with npm run test:pg (embedded-postgres) because PGlite serializes transactions.

Each module runs its Playwright tests with its own e2ePort, PGLITE_DIR=.data/pglite-e2e-<id> and NEXT_DIST_DIR=.next-e2e-<id> to avoid collisions in the shared working tree; run next typegen (through scripts/heavy.sh tsc) after adding a route that was not a placeholder.
Schema changes are never made by modules: write docs/schema-requests/<module-id>.md instead.
No agent commits; the orchestrator commits after each phase.
